# PEN-4990 — assert WHICH containers receive the github.com credential

PR: [#3103](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3103)

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.github-credential-container-set.test.ts` (new)

## What changed

A test only. No production source under this adapter is touched.

It renders the agent Job in four arrangements — broker off/on, each with and
without DinD — walks every container in the assembled pod spec, and pins an
exact map of container to the github.com credential routes it receives. Two
route kinds are reported separately:

- the Secret volume mount, matched both by mount path
  (`/etc/paperclip/secrets/github-*token`) and by Secret name
  (`paperclip-github-*token`), and counting a mount at any ANCESTOR of a
  credential path as reaching it;
- the env route, split into the `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE` pointer and the
  four credential-bearing names §7.4 keeps refused.

## Why

PEN-3183 §7.2 trigger 3 is "any change that widens read access to the token
Secret, or mounts it into a new container". Its `/etc/gitconfig` half is
asserted twice over; the mount half was asserted nowhere, so adding the Secret
to a new container was caught only by human review.

`job-manifest.github-publish-broker.test.ts` is the closest existing check and
is a different one: it asserts the two containers it already knows about (agent
must not hold the credential, broker must) and nothing about the SET, so a
third container with the Secret mounted into it leaves every case in that file
green. Verified by mutation: mounting the credential into the DinD sidecar, and
restoring it to the agent under the broker, each red the new file.

Both broker arrangements are expectations rather than one, because §7.2 says
the broker receiving a credential IS trigger 3 — a declared, reviewed instance
of it. A test written against only the pre-broker shape would red the PEN-4933
rollout.

The matchers are restated in the test rather than imported from
`isGitHubCredentialSecretVolume`. That predicate is what decides the diversion
and its failure direction is OPEN; a test sharing it would go green on the day
it stopped matching.

The fixture's second credential volume is named `paperclip-github-second-token`,
not the real seat token. Only `paperclip-github-mcp-token` is on
`AGENT_SECRET_VOLUME_ALLOWLIST` and the filter runs at capture time, so a second
volume cannot occur in production; feeding one past that filter keeps the
assertion about "every credential volume" rather than one hard-coded path,
while a fixture named after the seat token would have read as a claim that
BLO-24056's removal had been undone.

The test is DIRECTION-BLIND and says so in its own header: it reds on a
credential route being removed exactly as on one being added. That is accepted
for a merge gate — a human reads the diff — and is the same limitation the
`/etc/gitconfig` assertions carry.

## Review round 2 (#3103)

Review found the route predicate too narrow, and it was right: matching mounts
by path or by `volumes[].secret.secretName`, and env routes by VARIABLE NAME,
gave a green for three complete routes to the token —
`env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef` under any name at all,
`envFrom[].secretRef`, and a `projected` volume mounted at a
non-credential path.

That is a LIVE path for this adapter, not a hypothetical. `k8s-client.ts`
captures the Deployment container's `valueFrom` entries and its allowlisted
`envFrom` sources — filtered by env NAME only, never by which Secret they
reference — and `job-manifest.ts` emits both into the agent container. The
first draft set `inheritedEnvValueFrom` / `inheritedEnvFrom` to `[]` in the
fixture, so the path was never exercised.

Added: a `secretRefs` route bucket matching the referenced SECRET rather than
the variable name; `projected` volume sources folded into the volume->Secret
map; and a case that feeds a `secretKeyRef` to `paperclip-github-mcp-token`
under the name `MY_TOKEN` — a name that appears in no list in the file — plus
an `envFrom` secretRef, asserting both land on the agent container. Verified by
mutation: neutering `secretRefRoutes` reds that case.

Worth recording for the next reader: this adapter does NOT re-apply the env
name allowlist at build time, trusting the capture-time filter. The
opencode_k8s adapter does re-apply it. Neither is wrong — capture is the
control — but the asymmetry is real and is now pinned by a test on each side.
